blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from Jared's verified local notes (researched November 1, 2026). Listing-stated figures are labelled; unconfirmed items say so. No live listing feed or board statistics are attached to this page yet.

Agassiz is the principal community and service centre of the District of Kent, on the north bank of the Fraser River at the foot of Mount Cheam's valley wall, along Highway 7 (Lougheed) and Highway 9; Municipal Hall is at 7170 Cheam Avenue and Pioneer Avenue is the main street, with grocery, pharmacy and services in the townsite. The townsite is compact and flat, ringed by ALR farmland, and growth is deliberately directed into the existing townsite to keep it compact and protect farmland.
This guide covers Agassiz's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.

items.t: Agassiz is the principal community and service centre of the District of Kent, on the north bank of the Fraser River at the foot of Mount Cheam's valley wall, along Highway 7 (Lougheed) and Highway 9; Municipal Hall is at 7170 Cheam Avenue and Pioneer Avenue is the main street, with grocery, pharmacy and services in the townsite. The townsite is compact and flat, ringed by ALR farmland, and growth is deliberately directed into the existing townsite to keep it compact and protect farmland.

Board position: Agassiz is a CADREB board community with its own MLS® area name (Harrison Mills is a sub-area under it), and CADREB publishes board-wide statistics only, so no board stats package exists for Agassiz. The SnapStats FVR September 2026 report covers Surrey, S Surrey White Rock, North Delta, Cloverdale, Langley, Abbotsford and Mission only — there is no Agassiz or Kent row, and all Agassiz market figures are not verified from that source.

Where condo stock concentrates: the townsite's strata stock is townhouse form, clustered on the Mackay Crescent / Heath Road / Morrow Road streets around the core — Village Gate and The Langtry on Mackay Crescent, Gallagher Landing and Town Centre Gable on Heath Road, Fraser Green on the Agassiz-Rosedale Highway and the Morrow Road complexes to the south.
The Agassiz Centre for Education (alternate, grades 8–12) shares the 7110 Cheam Avenue site.

Transit: BC Transit Route 71 (Agassiz–Harrison) runs Chilliwack–Rosedale–Agassiz–Harrison Hot Springs, and Route 72 (Hope) runs Agassiz–Hope via Highway 7; Agassiz (Pioneer Ave at Evergreen Dr) is the transfer point between them, and the FVRD administers both routes. Service is limited — check schedules per trip.

Healthcare is a Fraser Health community cluster, not a hospital: the Agassiz Public Health Unit at 7243 Pioneer Avenue, the Agassiz Community Health Centre at 7040 Cheam Avenue, plus Agassiz Home Health and the Agassiz Mental Health and Substance Use Centre. No hospital in Agassiz.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Agassiz

items.t: Municipal law here is District of Kent law, not "Agassiz" law: zoning is the District of Kent Zoning Bylaw No. 1219, 2001 (as amended); the plan is the District of Kent Official Community Plan 2025, which designates the townsite core "Commercial – Town Centre" and directs growth into the townsite. Kent Bylaw No. 1737, adopted June 10, 2024, created the RS1 zone, under which serviced residential lots in Agassiz can take up to four dwelling units without rezoning, subject to conditions; the District also permits secondary suites in single-family homes in all residential zones. (55+ notes

Floodplain rules: Agassiz sits on the Fraser River floodplain behind dikes. Flood Protection & Erosion is OCP Section 5.5; the District has a Floodplain Bylaw that applications must comply with, plus area-specific flood construction levels — there is no single townsite-wide FCL in the sources checked, so the FCL is a per-property check. The local system includes Maria Slough and the Hammersley, Kilby and Bateson pump stations.

District of Kent taxes — District figures only: taxes are District of Kent municipal taxes (there is no separate "Agassiz" tax bill). The District's 2026 schedule (per $1,000 of taxable value) sets the Class 1 Residential total municipal rate at 2.80493, plus a separate dyking line of 0.03076, for an all-in residential total of 4.65328 including hospital, regional district, MFA, BC Assessment and school tax. Notices are mailed in early June and due July 15 (or the next business day), with penalties after.
Renting a unit out (landlord frame): RTB rent increases are capped at 2.3% for 2026 and 2.2% for 2027 for ordinary tenancies.

blocks.text: Good to know about Agassiz

items.t: The new aquatic centre just opened. The Lets'emot Regional Recreation & Aquatic Centre, beside the Community Recreation and Cultural Centre at 6660 Pioneer Avenue, opened to the public on September 25, 2026 — the grand opening date set in the District's September 9, 2026 council highlights; the District's FAQ had projected a late 2026 opening on a $25 million budget.

Diking is a line item, not a surprise. The District's 2026 Tax Rates Summary carries a dedicated "Dyking" column charged per $1,000 of taxable value — 0.03076 for Class 1 Residential — on top of the total municipal rate of 2.80493.

The pump station west of town was rebuilt with provincial money. The Province funded a $4.17 million upgrade of the Hammersley Pump Station, about 6 km west of Agassiz, part of the flood system the townsite depends on.

The District is planning for a lot more homes — mostly in this townsite. Kent's Interim Housing Needs Report (2024), as presented in its OCP update, found 495 new homes needed immediately and 1,695 more by 2041, with growth directed mainly to the Agassiz townsite and Mount Woodside; the 2025 OCP update emphasizes gentle-density infill in the townsite and more homes in the Town Centre. (55+ notes

Both seniors care campuses changed hands in 2018. Park Place Seniors Living acquired Agassiz Seniors Community (previously Cheam Village) and Glenwood Seniors Community on September 6, 2018 — pre-2018 directories listing "Cheam Village" or "Glenwood Care Centre" describe these same two buildings under old names. (55+ notes

The townsite's strata names cluster in a few blocks. The two Park Place care campuses, the two subsidized seniors buildings and several of the townsite's strata complexes (Village Gate and The Langtry on Mackay Crescent among them) all sit in the MacKay Crescent / Morrow Road / McCaffrey Road side of the townsite — the seniors and strata geography of Agassiz is a few-blocks story. (55+ notes
There is no hospital in Agassiz. Fraser Health lists community and public-health services only for Agassiz — a buyer pricing in on-site hospital care is misreading the service cluster.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Agassiz
What trades here

items.t: What land actually trades here: infill within the townsite (single-family and townhouse) per the OCP's compact-growth direction, plus acreages and farmhouses outside the townsite boundary on the farm plain.
Fee-simple lots — the default form: freehold dominates in Agassiz; a fee-simple lot carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees.
: They are built townhouse stock, named here only so a land reader does not mistake them for lot inventory.

ALR edge: some townsite-area Residential–Future lands are currently in the ALR and stay in farm use until an ALC exclusion is approved, with a Council-approved Neighbourhood Plan required first — "future residential" on a plan map is therefore not a buyable building lot today. Exact ALR share of the District lands around the townsite: Not verified.

items.t: Nearby areas: Harrison Hot Springs (north, ~10 min), Harrison Mills (west, in Kent), Rosedale (south across the Agassiz-Rosedale Bridge, in Chilliwack), Seabird Island and Sts'ailes (First Nations communities adjoining), and Mount Woodside (the in-Kent growth area). Highway 9 crosses the Fraser at the Agassiz-Rosedale Bridge to Chilliwack and Highway 1; Highway 7 runs west to Mission and east to Hope. Timed drives: Not verified.

The SnapStats FVR September 2026 report covers Surrey, S Surrey White Rock, North Delta, Cloverdale, Langley, Abbotsford and Mission only; there is no Agassiz or Kent row, and CADREB publishes no area stats.

Land shape: the townsite is compact and flat, ringed by ALR farmland; growth is deliberately directed into the existing townsite to keep it compact and protect farmland, and the flat District lands outside the townsite are predominantly farm. Standard small-town residential lots sit in the townsite; acreages sit in the surrounding farm plain.

Schools (SD78 Fraser-Cascade, Ministry-listed names): Kent Elementary School (K–6), 7285 McCullough Road; Agassiz Elementary-Secondary School (grades 7–12), 7110 Cheam Avenue, serving the District of Kent, the Village of Harrison Hot Springs and the Sts'ailes, Seabird Island, Cheam and Scowlitz communities, with Kent Elementary and Harrison Hot Springs Elementary as its feeder schools; the Agassiz Centre for Education (alternate, grades 8–12) shares the 7110 Cheam Avenue site. SD78's Policy 7000 defines the AESS catchment as all grade 7–12 students in Kent and Harrison Hot Springs, plus the area east of the Chehalis watershed boundary, west of Ruby Creek (Hwy 7) and south to the Fraser River. Address-level catchments beyond that policy statement: Not verified without a district confirmation for the exact address.

Census note (Statistics Canada, 2021): no separate census count exists for "Agassiz" — the census subdivision is Kent: 6,300 people in 2,351 of 2,518 total private dwellings, up 3.8% from 6,067 in 2016 (census land area 168.59 km², density 37.4/km²). The District's own documents state a total area of 19,374 ha — a different measurement basis from the census land area.

items.t: OCP — District of Kent Official Community Plan 2025: (the District's current OCP; an update process continued into early 2026), which designates the townsite core "Commercial – Town Centre" and directs growth into the townsite. Harrison Hot Springs' OCP 1184, 2022 belongs to the Village of Harrison Hot Springs only and is NOT a Kent number.

SSMUH — District of Kent, as its own: the 2025 OCP update notes small-scale multi-unit housing can allow up to four units on serviced residential lots without rezoning, subject to conditions. Whether the four-unit position applies to a given lot is per-parcel.
Subdivision and servicing — District of Kent / FVRD servicing bylaw numbers not verified: (Standing verified ledger, applied by exclusion.)

Floodplain rules: the District has a Floodplain Bylaw its applications must comply with, and area-specific flood construction levels (e.g., 19.0 m GSC for the Gateway lands — not townsite-wide); OCP policy is a minimum finished-floor elevation from the latest flood elevations plus freeboard. There is no single townsite-wide FCL in the sources checked, so the FCL is a per-property check: Not verified at parcel level.

Property taxes — District of Kent (a municipality; follow its own research): taxes are District of Kent municipal taxes — there is no separate "Agassiz" tax bill. The District's 2026 schedule (per $1,000 of taxable value) sets the Class 1 Residential total municipal rate at 2.80493, plus a separate dyking line of 0.03076, for an all-in residential total of 4.65328 including hospital, regional district, MFA, BC Assessment and school tax. Notices are mailed in early June and due July 15 (or the next business day), with penalties after.

faq.q: Are there any apartment condos to buy in Agassiz?
faq.a: None verified. Fresh verification by name found every named townsite strata complex to be townhouse form — Village Gate, The Langtry, Fraser Green, Gallagher Landing, Town Centre Gable, MountView and Huckleberry Lane — and no apartment-form building could be verified by name on a public source.

faq.q: Is there a 55+ condo or townhouse I can buy in Agassiz?
faq.a: No verified one. No public source states a 55+ age bylaw for any Agassiz strata complex — treat any "55+" claim for an Agassiz strata as not confirmed until the strata's registered bylaws are in hand; one fresh listing states the opposite for Huckleberry Lane ("no age restrictions"). The verified seniors stock in town is rental and care, not ownership. (55+ notes

faq.q: Are there any market statistics for Agassiz?
faq.a: No published package: SnapStats FVR has no Agassiz or Kent row, and CADREB publishes board-wide statistics only.

faq.q: Can I rent out an Agassiz townhouse long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, including the restriction element in Town Centre Gable's directory line. A strata can still restrict short-term rentals by bylaw.

Yes — the townsite is diked Fraser River floodplain. The local system includes Maria Slough and the Hammersley, Kilby and Bateson pump stations, the District has a Floodplain Bylaw, and diking is a visible separate line on the tax schedule. Confirm the flood construction level for the specific property before writing.

faq.q: What townhouses can I actually buy in Agassiz?
faq.a: Six verified strata complexes, all in the townsite: Village Gate and The Langtry on Mackay Crescent, Town Centre Gable on Heath Road, Fraser Green and MountView on the Agassiz-Rosedale Highway, and Huckleberry Lane on Morrow Road. Every one is strata — budget for strata fees and a Form B review.

faq.q: Are any Agassiz townhouses fee-simple (no strata)?
faq.a: None verified. The townsite's verified townhouse stock is entirely strata-titled; the fee-simple product here is detached houses, which are a different purchase.

faq.q: Is there a 55+ townhouse I can buy in Agassiz?
faq.a: No verified one. No public source states a 55+ age bylaw for any counted Agassiz townhouse complex — Huckleberry Lane's listing states "no age restrictions" — and the town's verified 55+ forms are a bare-land strata of detached ranchers (Maplewood Village, realtor-stated) and rental/care housing, not townhouses. Treat any "55+" claim for an Agassiz townhouse as not confirmed until the registered bylaws are in hand.

faq.q: What am I actually buying when I buy an "acreage" in Agassiz?
faq.a: A whole fee-simple farm-plain parcel or farmhouse outside the townsite boundary, predominantly ALR ground. There is no acreage subdivision, no bare-land strata and no presale acreage product to buy instead — each parcel is judged on its own title, Kent zoning and ALR status.

faq.q: The plan map shows Residential–Future land — can I buy and build there now?
faq.a: Not on the designation alone: some of those lands are currently in the ALR and stay in farm use until an ALC exclusion is approved, with a Council-approved Neighbourhood Plan required first.

faq.q: Is an Agassiz acreage in a floodplain, and is it serviced?
faq.a: Floodplain: yes in character — diked Fraser floodplain, with a District Floodplain Bylaw and area-specific flood construction levels; confirm the FCL for the specific property before writing. Servicing: Not confirmed per parcel — the four-unit SSMUH position covers serviced townsite lots, not farm parcels; confirm water/sewer/septic with the District for the exact parcel.

faq.q: Which schools serve an Agassiz acreage?
faq.a: Kent Elementary School (K–6, 7285 McCullough Road) and Agassiz Elementary-Secondary School (grades 7–12, 7110 Cheam Avenue), both SD78; SD78 Policy 7000 defines the AESS catchment as all grade 7–12 students in Kent and Harrison Hot Springs plus the defined surrounding area. Any address outside that policy statement needs a district confirmation.
